DILG DACONO P'LIP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph OILG OPINION NO. S. AUG 18 2025 ALLAN P. RAMBANO Provincial Legal Officer Catbalogan City, Province of Samar Dear Mr. Rambano: This refers to your Letter dated 19 June 2025, requesting this Department legal opinion on the following queries, which we quote verbatim: I. 2. 3. "Can the Provincial Govemment of Samar establish its own public market and public transport terminal?" "What are the necessary steps the Provincial Government of Samar has to take in order to construct and manage a public market and public terminal of its own?" "How can the Provincial Govemment of Samar get the authority to construct such establishments?" After a careful examination of the relevant laws and jurisprudence on the matter, this Department respectfully opines that the Province of Samar may be deemed impliedly authorized to establish and operate its own public market and public transport terminal, particularly when such facilities are provincial or inter-municipal in character and intended to promote the general welfare of its inhabitants. At the outset, we note that under Sections 447 and 458 of the Local Government Code (LGC), the express authority to establish public markets and transport terminals is granted to municipalities and cities. Section 468, which enumerates the powers of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, does not expressly include this authority. If read strictissimi juris, such omission may be construed as exclusion. However, this Department adopts a liberal construction of the relevant provisions, in harmony with Section 16 of the LGC (the general welfare clause). This provision empowers every LGU to exercise not only powers expressly granted but also those necessarily implied or incidental to the promotion of the general welfare, including the provision of facilities that support local commerce, enhance mobility, and improve the quality of life of residents, When a public market or transport terminal serves an inter-municipal or province-wide purpose—such as facilitating trade between component LGUs, providing centralized transport hubs, or addressing economic needs that transcend municipal boundaries— it may be considered within the corporate powers of the Province by necessary implication from the general welfare clause. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

To lawfully implement such a project, the Provincial Government should: 1. Establish that the facility's purpose and scope are provincial in nature; 2. Secure the enactment of an ordinance by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan providing authority, funding, and operational guidelines; 3. Coordinate with affected cities and municipalities to harmonize ordinances and avoid jurisdictional conflicts; and 4. Ensure compliance with all applicable national laws and regulations. In view of the foregoing, it is the considered opinion of this Department that the Provincial Government of Samar may establish, construct, operate, and manage public markets and transport terminals that are provincial or inter-municipal in character, by virtue of its implied authority under Section 16 of the LGC, subject to the conditions above. This legal opinion is rendered without prejudice to any contrary interpretation by competent authorities or the courts. We trust to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Ven,' truly yours, ATTY. ROMEO P. ENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLARPB/LLLSLRALLD/Pbf/kbrn Page 2 of2
